category_title: Non-symbolic communicators with quadriplegic cerebral palsy who use facial expressions and physical resistance to express preferences
minimal_context: Mary is supporting Tony's head and attempting to feed him with a spoon during mealtime.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for your meal, Tony. I am going to move to support your head now.

STUDENT: (Tony becomes tense at being handled. His eyes close, his tongue protrudes, and he looks nervous.)

TUTOR: Let's just get you set up. Here we go.

STUDENT: (Tony remains tense, keeping his eyes closed and looking nervous as his head is supported.)

TUTOR: Okay, I am going to try to feed you with this spoon now. Here comes the food.

STUDENT: (Tony pushes his tongue out and forces the spoon away from his mouth.)

options.A: Offer a trip to the park as a reward after completing the feeding activity.
options.B: Play the music of W. A. Mozart in the background during the feeding activity.
options.C: Utilize established routines and learned patterns of behavior that are predictable during the feeding activity.
options.D: Review Tony's Thumbs Up sheet and have him count the circled thumbs up and thumbs down.
